one_sentence: This document argues that a six-step logical chain, mapped to physics, necessarily converges on substitutionary atonement as the only solution to the justice-mercy paradox.
executive_summary: This document presents a six-step logical chain that begins with the universal human belief in good and evil and ends with the necessity of substitutionary atonement. Each step is mapped to a physical law: moral realism to electromagnetic truth, free will to a consciousness threshold, mixed moral nature to native duality, the need for salvation to thermodynamic entropy, ultimate justice to conservation laws, and the justice-mercy paradox to quantum entanglement. The conclusion is that only one historical event—the substitution of a perfectly aligned being—satisfies both perfect justice and perfect mercy. The document further demonstrates convergence by showing that the same chain can be derived independently from logic, physics, and scripture, with a Shannon information content of 43.6 bits indicating a 1 in 17 trillion probability of chance alignment.
short_summary: This document is a logical proof that substitutionary atonement is the only mathematically necessary solution to the justice-mercy paradox. The core structural claim is that six steps, from universal moral belief to the need for a substitute, form an unbreakable chain. Key evidence includes mappings to physical laws (e.g., entropy, quantum entanglement) and a three-way convergence proof from logic, physics, and scripture. This matters because it grounds a central theological doctrine in objective, cross-disciplinary necessity.
